# [Writing a Custom Provider](https://ai-sdk.dev/providers/openai-compatible-providers/custom-providers\#writing-a-custom-provider)

You can create your own provider package that leverages the AI SDK's [OpenAI Compatible package](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@ai-sdk/openai-compatible). Publishing your provider package to [npm](https://www.npmjs.com/) can give users an easy way to use the provider's models and stay up to date with any changes you may have. Here's an example structure:

### [File Structure](https://ai-sdk.dev/providers/openai-compatible-providers/custom-providers\#file-structure)

```bash
1packages/example/

2├── src/

3│   ├── example-chat-settings.ts       # Chat model types and settings

4│   ├── example-completion-settings.ts # Completion model types and settings

5│   ├── example-embedding-settings.ts  # Embedding model types and settings

6│   ├── example-image-settings.ts      # Image model types and settings

7│   ├── example-provider.ts            # Main provider implementation

8│   ├── example-provider.test.ts       # Provider tests

9│   └── index.ts                       # Public exports

10├── package.json

11├── tsconfig.json

12├── tsup.config.ts                     # Build configuration

13└── README.md
```

### [Key Files](https://ai-sdk.dev/providers/openai-compatible-providers/custom-providers\#key-files)

1. **example-chat-settings.ts** \- Define chat model IDs and settings:

```ts
1export type ExampleChatModelId =

2  | 'example/chat-model-1'

3  | 'example/chat-model-2'

4  | (string & {});
```

The completion, embedding, and image settings are implemented similarly to the chat settings.

2. **example-provider.ts** \- Main provider implementation:

```ts
1import { LanguageModelV4, EmbeddingModelV4 } from '@ai-sdk/provider';

2import {

3  OpenAICompatibleChatLanguageModel,

4  OpenAICompatibleCompletionLanguageModel,

5  OpenAICompatibleEmbeddingModel,

6  OpenAICompatibleImageModel,

7} from '@ai-sdk/openai-compatible';

8import {

9  FetchFunction,

10  loadApiKey,

11  withoutTrailingSlash,

12} from '@ai-sdk/provider-utils';

13// Import your model id and settings here.

14

15export interface ExampleProviderSettings {

16  /**

17Example API key.

18*/

19  apiKey?: string;

20  /**

21Base URL for the API calls.

22*/

23  baseURL?: string;

24  /**

25Custom headers to include in the requests.

26*/

27  headers?: Record<string, string>;

28  /**

29Optional custom url query parameters to include in request urls.

30*/

31  queryParams?: Record<string, string>;

32  /**

33Custom fetch implementation. You can use it as a middleware to intercept requests,

34or to provide a custom fetch implementation for e.g. testing.

35*/

36  fetch?: FetchFunction;

37}

38

39export interface ExampleProvider {

40  /**

41Creates a model for text generation.

42*/

43  (

44    modelId: ExampleChatModelId,

45    settings?: ExampleChatSettings,

46  ): LanguageModelV4;

47

48  /**

49Creates a chat model for text generation.

50*/

51  chatModel(

52    modelId: ExampleChatModelId,

53    settings?: ExampleChatSettings,

54  ): LanguageModelV4;

55

56  /**

57Creates a completion model for text generation.

58*/

59  completionModel(

60    modelId: ExampleCompletionModelId,

61    settings?: ExampleCompletionSettings,

62  ): LanguageModelV4;

63

64  /**

65Creates a text embedding model for text generation.

66*/

67  .embeddingModel(

68    modelId: ExampleEmbeddingModelId,

69    settings?: ExampleEmbeddingSettings,

70  ): EmbeddingModelV4<string>;

71

72  /**

73Creates an image model for image generation.

74*/

75  imageModel(

76    modelId: ExampleImageModelId,

77    settings?: ExampleImageSettings,

78  ): ImageModelV4;

79}

80

81export function createExample(

82  options: ExampleProviderSettings = {},

83): ExampleProvider {

84  const baseURL = withoutTrailingSlash(

85    options.baseURL ?? 'https://api.example.com/v1',

86  );

87  const getHeaders = () => ({

88    Authorization: `Bearer ${loadApiKey({

89      apiKey: options.apiKey,

90      environmentVariableName: 'EXAMPLE_API_KEY',

91      description: 'Example API key',

92    })}`,

93    ...options.headers,

94  });

95

96  interface CommonModelConfig {

97    provider: string;

98    url: ({ path }: { path: string }) => string;

99    headers: () => Record<string, string>;

100    fetch?: FetchFunction;

101  }

102

103  const getCommonModelConfig = (modelType: string): CommonModelConfig => ({

104    provider: `example.${modelType}`,

105    url: ({ path }) => {

106      const url = new URL(`${baseURL}${path}`);

107      if (options.queryParams) {

108        url.search = new URLSearchParams(options.queryParams).toString();

109      }

110      return url.toString();

111    },

112    headers: getHeaders,

113    fetch: options.fetch,

114  });

115

116  const createChatModel = (

117    modelId: ExampleChatModelId,

118    settings: ExampleChatSettings = {},

119  ) => {

120    return new OpenAICompatibleChatLanguageModel(

121      modelId,

122      settings,

123      getCommonModelConfig('chat'),

124    );

125  };

126

127  const createCompletionModel = (

128    modelId: ExampleCompletionModelId,

129    settings: ExampleCompletionSettings = {},

130  ) =>

131    new OpenAICompatibleCompletionLanguageModel(

132      modelId,

133      settings,

134      getCommonModelConfig('completion'),

135    );

136

137  const create.embeddingModel = (

138    modelId: ExampleEmbeddingModelId,

139    settings: ExampleEmbeddingSettings = {},

140  ) =>

141    new OpenAICompatibleEmbeddingModel(

142      modelId,

143      settings,

144      getCommonModelConfig('embedding'),

145    );

146

147  const createImageModel = (

148    modelId: ExampleImageModelId,

149    settings: ExampleImageSettings = {},

150  ) =>

151    new OpenAICompatibleImageModel(

152      modelId,

153      settings,

154      getCommonModelConfig('image'),

155    );

156

157  const provider = (

158    modelId: ExampleChatModelId,

159    settings?: ExampleChatSettings,

160  ) => createChatModel(modelId, settings);

161

162  provider.completionModel = createCompletionModel;

163  provider.chatModel = createChatModel;

164  provider.embeddingModel = create.embeddingModel;

165  provider.imageModel = createImageModel;

166

167  return provider;

168}

169

170// Export default instance

171export const example = createExample();
```

3. **index.ts** \- Public exports:

```ts
1export { createExample, example } from './example-provider';

2export type {

3  ExampleProvider,

4  ExampleProviderSettings,

5} from './example-provider';
```

4. **package.json** \- Package configuration:

```js
1{

2  "name": "@company-name/example",

3  "version": "0.0.1",

4  "dependencies": {

5    "@ai-sdk/openai-compatible": "^0.0.7",

6    "@ai-sdk/provider": "^1.0.2",

7    "@ai-sdk/provider-utils": "^2.0.4",

8    // ...additional dependencies

9  },

10  // ...additional scripts and module build configuration

11}
```

### [Usage](https://ai-sdk.dev/providers/openai-compatible-providers/custom-providers\#usage)

Once published, users can use your provider like this:

```ts
1import { example } from '@company-name/example';

2import { generateText } from 'ai';

3

4const { text } = await generateText({

5  model: example('example/chat-model-1'),

6  prompt: 'Hello, how are you?',

7});
```

This structure provides a clean, type-safe implementation that leverages the OpenAI Compatible package while maintaining consistency with the usage of other AI SDK providers.

### [Internal API](https://ai-sdk.dev/providers/openai-compatible-providers/custom-providers\#internal-api)

As you work on your provider you may need to use some of the internal API of the OpenAI Compatible package. You can import these from the `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible/internal` package, for example:

```ts
1import { convertToOpenAICompatibleChatMessages } from '@ai-sdk/openai-compatible/internal';
```

You can see the latest available exports in the AI SDK [GitHub repository](https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/main/packages/openai-compatible/src/internal/index.ts).

web.title: Add Haimaker to OpenCode: Custom Provider Setup (2026)
web.markdown:
[SOVEREIGN](https://haimaker.ai/sovereign) DEVELOPER [Model API](https://haimaker.ai/model-api) [Dedicated Endpoints](https://haimaker.ai/dedicated-endpoints) [Batch Inference](https://haimaker.ai/batch-inference) [GPU Instances](https://haimaker.ai/gpu-instances) [GPU Clusters](https://haimaker.ai/gpu-clusters) [Managed Kubernetes](https://haimaker.ai/managed-kubernetes) [COMPUTE](https://haimaker.ai/compute) [START BUILDING NOW](https://app.haimaker.ai/sign-up?utm_source=blog_how-to-add-haimaker-opencode&utm_medium=marketing-website&utm_campaign=header)

![Add Haimaker to OpenCode: Custom Provider Setup (2026)](https://haimaker.ai/images/how-to-add-haimaker-opencode-hero.jpg)

OpenCode supports 75+ LLM providers out of the box, but what if you want to use a provider that isn’t in the directory? You can add any OpenAI-compatible API as a custom provider with a few lines of config.

This guide walks through adding [Haimaker](https://haimaker.ai/) — an inference routing platform that gives you access to dozens of models through a single API.

The fastest way to wire it in, with no config files to edit, is a single command:

```
export HAIMAKER_API_KEY=your-haimaker-key
npx -y @haimaker/connect --opencode
```

[`@haimaker/connect`](https://haimaker.ai/connect) writes the OpenCode provider block, stores your credential in the right place, verifies the connection, then exits — nothing of ours sits in the request path afterward. Add `--project` to write a project-local config instead of the global one, or `--pick-model` to choose a model interactively. Restart OpenCode and run `/models` to select a Haimaker model.

The same command also wires up Claude Code, Codex, OpenClaw, Hermes, Cline, and Kilo Code — see the [connect guide](https://haimaker.ai/connect) for every flag.

Prefer to see exactly what gets written, or want to wire up a provider the CLI doesn’t cover? The manual steps below do the same thing by hand.

## Why use a custom provider?

A few reasons you might want this:

- **Access to different models.** Haimaker routes to models you won’t find on other platforms, including cost-optimized and specialized options.
- **Cost control.** Route by price, latency, or compliance requirements. Haimaker is typically 5% cheaper than comparable providers.
- **Single API key.** One key, many models. Less config sprawl.

## Step 1: Get your Haimaker API key

1. Sign up at [haimaker.ai](https://haimaker.ai/)
2. Grab your API key from the dashboard

## Step 2: Configure the provider

OpenCode uses a config file to define custom providers. Open (or create) your config at:

```
~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc
```

Add Haimaker as a provider:

```
{
  "provider": {
    "haimaker": {
      "npm": "@ai-sdk/openai-compatible",
      "options": {
        "baseURL": "https://api.haimaker.ai/v1"
      },
      "models": {
        "z-ai/glm-4.6": {}
      }
    }
  }
}
```

A few notes:

- The `npm` field tells OpenCode to use the OpenAI-compatible SDK adapter
- `baseURL` points to Haimaker’s API endpoint
- `models` lists which models you want available — add more as needed

## Step 3: Add your API key

OpenCode stores credentials separately from config. Add your Haimaker key to:

```
~/.local/share/opencode/auth.json
```

```
{
  "haimaker": {
    "type": "api",
    "key": "HAIMAKER_API_KEY"
  }
}
```

Replace `HAIMAKER_API_KEY` with the actual key from your dashboard.

## Step 4: Select a model

Run OpenCode and use the `/models` command to switch to your Haimaker model. You should see `haimaker/z-ai/glm-4.6` (or whatever models you configured) in the list.

## Adding more models

Haimaker gives you access to a bunch of models. Check the [model hub](https://haimaker.ai/models) to see what’s available, then add them to your config:

```
{
  "provider": {
    "haimaker": {
      "npm": "@ai-sdk/openai-compatible",
      "options": {
        "baseURL": "https://api.haimaker.ai/v1"
      },
      "models": {
        "z-ai/glm-4.6": {},
        "anthropic/claude-3-5-sonnet": {},
        "openai/gpt-4o": {},
        "meta-llama/llama-3.1-405b": {}
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Model IDs follow the format on Haimaker’s model hub. Copy them exactly.

## Troubleshooting

**“Model not found” error**
Double-check the model ID matches what’s in Haimaker’s model hub. Case and formatting matter.

**Authentication failed**
Make sure `auth.json` has the right structure and your API key is valid. You can test your key with a quick curl:

```
curl https://api.haimaker.ai/v1/models \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer HAIMAKER_API_KEY"
```

**Provider not showing up**
Restart OpenCode after editing config files. Changes aren’t picked up automatically.

* * *

This same pattern works for any OpenAI-compatible API. Just swap the `baseURL` and model names.

Questions? Hit us up in [Discord](https://discord.gg/6fG89cbZ).
